newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia says 39 firms interested in ZCCM assets. [CORRECTED 09:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Zambia says 39 firms interested in ZCCM assets. [CORRECTED 09:12 GMT]

text.p: The Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Thursday it had a pre-qualification shortlist of 39 companies interested in the assets of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM), which is up for privatisation.
(ZCCM corrects number of companies shortlisted, in title and throughout.)

"Following an invitation published in the international press, a total of 39 companies have pre-qualified for the sale by international tender of majority interests in ZCCM assets," ZPA technical director Stewart Cruickshank told Reuters.

He said of the 39 companies, 33 companies pre-qualified either individually or as part of a bidding group for one or more of the mining and treatment packages, while six had pre-qualified for the ZCCM Power Division.
Cruickshank said the number of successful pre-qualification bidders had increased to 39 from 21 in mid-October and could increase further by the time the exercise was completed.
"We are quite surprised by this increase in just two weeks," he said.
"A small number of prequalification applications are still being processed and the names of any further companies admitted to the tender will be released at a later date."
ZCCM chairman Luke Mwanashiku said the company was pleased that the prequalified companies represented a cross section of mining houses.
"We are particularly encouraged to see that the packages on offer have attracted not only most of the world's largest mining companies, but also the mid-tier and junior players," he said.
Companies that had prequalified represented a broad geographical spread and included bidders from the United States, Canada, Australia, South Africa, China, India, Belgium, the UK, Japan and Zambia.
Prequalified companies now have four months to conduct due diligence investigations into ZCCM's assets prior to submitting bids by February 28 for all assets except Kansanshi mine.
Bids for Kansanshi mine are due by November 29, 1996.
